adu.value: Not by right in R-7.5(A). An accessory dwelling unit needs either a Board of Adjustment special exception (51A-4.209(b)(6), about $600 fee, owner-occupancy deed restriction, rental registration) or a lot in an ADU Overlay (51A-4.510). trees.value: Article X (51A-10): protected trees removed must be replaced inch-for-inch (replacement 2 in caliper or more). New single-family lots need at least three 2-in trees, two of them in front. Single-family or duplex lots of 1 acre or less are exempt for trees in the 'unrestricted zone' (outside required setbacks or 15 ft from property lines, whichever is greater). A tree survey (6 in caliper or more, within 50 ft of construction) goes with the permit.

flood.value: Floodplain (51A-5.100): when filling in the floodplain, the lowest floor must be at least 3 ft above the design flood elevation and the building pad filled to at least 2 ft above it. In 500-year flood areas the lowest floor must be at least 3 ft above the 100-year elevation. Mechanical equipment must be at least 3 ft above the design flood elevation. Areas protected by Trinity/Elm Fork levees need 1 ft above the design flood. Habitable homes on piers in the floodplain are prohibited.

plainLanguage: Dallas builds homes under the 2021 International Residential Code with city amendments (Chapter 57). Every new house needs a foundation designed and stamped by a Texas engineer, because Dallas clay soils swell and shrink. In the common R-7.5(A) district the house must sit 25 ft back from the street and 5 ft from the side and rear lines. It can be up to 30 ft tall and cover up to 45% of the lot. Your subdivision plat, a Planned Development or a Conservation District can set stricter rules, so check your zoning first. The city cannot require brick or stone percentages on a normal lot, but HOAs and deed restrictions still can. Removing protected trees means replacing them inch-for-inch, and new homes need at least three trees. Dallas charges no impact fee; the building permit for a 2,400 sq ft house is roughly $1,000 before trade fees. A backyard cottage (ADU) is not allowed by right in most single-family areas.
